title: How he got the nickname Chinee
summary: Foster explains that playing in white and colored bands as a long-haired boy, people took him for Mexican, Spanish or Indian, and a 'Chinee' act on a show gave him the name.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: You see, when I first started, as I told you once before, I was a little kid. I'll be 61 on the 19th of March, St. Joseph Cummins. Born 1900, I'm with the year. Well, I got the name of Chai Nee by playing with white and colored bands. See, when I was a little boy, well, musicians wasn't like you are today. Musicians were very sketchy. They didn't have jukeboxes and different things like that. Well, when I was a little boy, I used to play with white and colored bands, as I told you. And so, half of them thought I was Mexican, half of them thought I was Spanish, half of them thought I was Puerto Rican, you see. Well, at that time, children used to have long hair and things like that, you see. And so, well, I started playing around the Latin Slager market with different bands, like I told you, white and colored. So they didn't know whether I was white or what I was colored. Some of them used to think I was Indian, just like Lorenzo Teo, the great clarinet player, like I told you. So they all started picking names and things like that. And so, one time I went on the show, and I done a Charni act. So from that on, white and colored started calling me Charni. A lot of people would say, well, how do you call him Charni? He goes, Charni, a gentleman is not dark like him. They say, well, he do that Charni act so good, so we just call him Charni. And from that time on, up until now, well, they've been calling me Charni. And very few know my right name.
